panels.rationale: Single-panel plain radiograph of both hands from an RS3PE case report. Caption and in-text confirm soft tissue swelling, extensor tenosynovitis, and synovitis without bone erosion in a patient diagnosed with RS3PE syndrome, matching the nonerosive polyarthritis radiographic pattern classic for RS3PE. No third-party copyright indicated; prior triage kept the figure.

in_text_mentions: ESR, although the RF, antinuclear antibodies, and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody levels were normal (Table 1). Furthermore, a radiograph of the hand showed synovitis without bone erosion (Figure 1). Upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) showed no abnormalities, including malignancy. He was diagnosed with RS3PE syndrome and received 20 mg/day of prednisolone (PSL), to which he responded well, and the laboratory data subsequently normalized. panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a real patient showing bilateral pitting dorsal hand edema with symmetrical synovitis of the wrists and MCP joints; the caption explicitly attributes the presentation to RS3PE syndrome ('Clinical presentation of RS3PE syndrome. Bilateral pitting edema of the hands with symmetrical synovitis involving the wrists and metacarpophalangeal joints'), matching the classic boxing-glove hand edema phenotype. Prior caption triage also classified it as a real patient RS3PE clinical photo with no third-party indication. Skin is adequately lit and shows medium tone with chronic sun-damaged elderly hands; no ethnicity or specific patient age stated in caption or in-text, so ethnicity is null and age group is inferred as older adult from visible elderly hands plus in-text statement that RS3PE typically affects elderly individuals.

in_text_mentions: RS3PE is a rare inflammatory syndrome typically affecting elderly individuals and characterized by symmetrical synovitis and pitting edema of the hands. It has been associated with various malignancies, highlighting the importance of malignancy screening in these patients [4,5]. Clinical findings are demonstrated in Figure 4.
